doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Listening habits and football
summary: He listens to jazz radio, older big bands and Coltrane, and chats about football and band sports teams.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Do you listen to a lot of music these days?
Yeah we have a station, Miami University, they have a jazz station and they play good jazz all day long.
Do you hear new stuff that you like, that perks your ear up.
Every now and then. Basically stuff like Basie, Jimmy Lunceford, Benny Goodman, John Coltrane, you know people like that. It’s background. Until I turn on the T.V. and I turn it off.
Until that game’s on.
Yeah and that’s that.
Which is your favorite sport?
My favorite sport is football.
Yeah. So we’ll know tomorrow, if you run off the stage, that you’ll be going up to your room to check on the football game. Right?
Oh definitely, yeah.
Who is your team these days?
I like the Green Bay Packers.
Yeah?
But you know the number one team is Colorado, isn’t it?
Yeah, well Denver, right?
Yeah.
Undefeated. Yeah. I’m a fan too.
Are you? Okay.
I’m a Giants fan which isn’t very much fun a lot.
Yeah, I know. But you know Green Bay, they’ve done pretty good. They lost two games so far.
Well it’s a good pastime.
Yeah it is.
And I know a lot of musicians are sports fans, in fact some of the big bands used to actually have little baseball teams.
Oh, yeah, that’s right. Duke had one. Basie had one too I think, a softball team. Do you like basketball?
Yes sir.
Yeah, me too. Chicago?
Celtics. Again, not a good team to root for in the last few years. But got to be a fan and stick with it.
Oh, yeah.
